item.title: Man's Search for Meaning
item.description:
Man’s Search for Meaning by Viktor E. Frankl

Summary

“Man’s Search for Meaning” is a profound memoir and psychological exploration written by Viktor E. Frankl, a neurologist, psychiatrist, and Holocaust survivor. The book is divided into two main parts. The first part details Frankl’s harrowing experiences in Nazi concentration camps during World War II, where he endured extreme suffering and witnessed the suffering of others. Through these experiences, Frankl develops his existential analysis, known as logotherapy, which forms the second part of the book.

item.title: The Will to Meaning: Foundations and Applications of Logotherapy
item.description:
The Will to Meaning: Foundations and Applications of Logotherapy

Summary

“The Will to Meaning” by Viktor E. Frankl is an exploration of logotherapy, which is a form of existential analysis that emphasizes the search for life’s meaning as the central human motivational force. The book delves into the philosophical and psychological underpinnings of logotherapy, discussing its application in various therapeutic settings. Frankl argues that the primary drive in human beings is not the pursuit of pleasure or power, but the quest for meaning, which can be found in every aspect of life, even in suffering.
